reasons: Status is correctly characterized: p0109–p0116 is a pure 'AS IS' disclaimer of all warranties 'WHETHER EXPRESS OR IMPLIED' with an express statement that nonconformity to Documentation may not be corrected, i.e. the playbook walk-away position, so a deviation/insert finding is warranted.

The redline is directionally correct and actionable: it inserts an affirmative limited warranty (workmanlike services, 12-month conformity to Documentation, compliance with laws, no malicious code) with a repair/replace/refund remedy, tracking the model language and the preferred 12-month software period, and uses the agreement's defined terms (Licensed Software, Licensed Technology, Documentation, Licensor, Licensee) correctly.

The disclaimer is properly subordinated: the 'EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THE LIMITED WARRANTY ABOVE' lead-in is added at the head of the disclaimer sentence that runs from p0110 into p0111, so the blanket disclaimer of express warranties no longer swallows the new warranty; the 0.598 changed-character ratio on p0110 reflects only the carve-out prefix plus unchanged original text, which is the minimum edit that achieves the position.
Comment is accurate, correctly attributed to us as Licensee, concise and in the required voice, states what changed and why, and offers the 90-day fallback consistent with the rule.

Minor (non-blocking) gap to consider on the next pass: the residual sentence at p0115–p0116 ('...OR THAT ERRORS ... OR NONCONFORMITY TO ITS DOCUMENTATION CAN OR WILL BE CORRECTED') may sit outside the carve-out if it is a separate sentence and could be argued to undercut the repair remedy; a parallel 'Except as expressly set forth above' qualifier there (and retitling the heading to 'LIMITED WARRANTY AND WARRANTY DISCLAIMER') would tighten the edit.
